definition.text: Evaluation Data is the record an evaluation produces -- scores, test results, and human feedback -- not the gate that consumes it (contrast card 7.3 Evaluate (Blind), a distinct card in this reference model). The evidence gathered here names three scored layers, not the four-dimension taxonomy an earlier draft of this card cited to the wrong page (see gaps): "An agent turns one user request into a sequence: model calls, tool calls, retries, sometimes subagents. Evaluation has to cover three layers, and they answer different questions." -- final-answer, trajectory, and per-turn (production) evaluation. A separate, sourced convention treats the produced verdict the same way -- as something to carry, not something to perform: OpenTelemetry's GenAI semantic conventions name "gen_ai.evaluation.result: records quality evaluation results via gen_ai.evaluation.score.value and gen_ai.evaluation.score.label" -- a carrier attribute, not an evaluator.

evidence.quote: An agent turns one user request into a sequence: model calls, tool calls, retries, sometimes subagents. Evaluation has to cover three layers, and they answer different questions.
gen_ai.evaluation.result: records quality evaluation results via gen_ai.evaluation.score.value and gen_ai.evaluation.score.label

standards.role: defines the attribute a produced evaluation verdict travels on -- gen_ai.evaluation.result -- so a score is comparable across collectors regardless of which framework produced it.
standards.covers: does not perform the evaluation, define a rubric, or decide pass/fail -- the same source that names the carrier only says it "records quality evaluation results via gen_ai.evaluation.score.value and gen_ai.evaluation.score.label": a carrier attribute, not an evaluation engine.

evidence.text: This is the standard cap-evaluation's own skill.json names for the same carrier, cited here to its underlying source.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.note: This repo actually runs Langfuse (observe-langfuse-web-1, observe-langfuse-worker-1, observe-postgres-1, per PASS.md A1) and Langfuse ships its own evals/scoring feature alongside tracing -- but PASS.md's own container inventory documents only trace ingestion and async trace processing, never evals; nothing gathered here confirms the evals half of Langfuse is exercised in this repo.

evidence.text: Cited for what Langfuse the platform provides, from Langfuse's own homepage (an earlier draft cited this same description to a docs/observability/overview URL that does not carry it -- see gaps); this repo's own running use of it is documented for tracing only (see gaps).

evidence.quote: Trace, evaluate, and improve AI agents with one open platform. Use production data to understand behavior, collaborate on fixes, and ship better quality at lower cost and latency.

tools.name: DeepEval
tools.note: A named evaluation-data framework distinct from a tracing platform: pytest-style test cases, reusable metrics and thresholds, run in CI, producing exactly the kind of stored test result this card names.

evidence.text: Not part of this repo's own stack; cited as a real implementation of the data shape this card describes.

evidence.quote: It works like Pytest for LLM applications, with test cases, reusable metrics, assertions, thresholds, and a runner designed for local development and CI/CD.

tools.name: MCPEval
tools.note: A research implementation scoring agent behaviour specifically over MCP tool-use patterns and external service calls, a narrower and more recent entrant than DeepEval.

evidence.text: Not part of this repo's own stack; cited to show the tool landscape is not limited to one shape of framework.

evidence.quote: We introduce MCPEval, an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based framework that automates end-to-end task generation and deep evaluation of LLM agents across diverse domains.

landscape.text: The real tradeoff inside 'evaluation data' is cost and variance versus coverage, and it falls on the boundary between automated and human-produced scores: "Run offline evaluations on datasets before shipping changes and online evaluations on sampled production traffic after. Use deterministic code checks for anything decidable, LLM-as-a-judge for semantic judgments, and human annotation to calibrate both." That same held-out-sample practice is also how a regression is caught at all: "Run a curated benchmark against every candidate version in CI and gate the release on the results." Both quotes describe evaluation output as something compared against a prior baseline or a human check, not a number computed once and discarded -- which is what makes it data rather than a one-time verdict.

evidence.quote: Run offline evaluations on datasets before shipping changes and online evaluations on sampled production traffic after. Use deterministic code checks for anything decidable, LLM-as-a-judge for semantic judgments, and human annotation to calibrate both.
Run a curated benchmark against every candidate version in CI and gate the release on the results.

usage.text: The shape of a written evaluation record is a scored trajectory compared against a stored baseline, not a bare pass/fail: "Run a curated benchmark against every candidate version in CI and gate the release on the results." The score itself carries the same three layers this card's own definition now names -- final-answer, trajectory, and per-turn, not the four-dimension taxonomy an earlier draft cited to the wrong page (see gaps) -- for example: "Trajectory evaluation. Score the sequence of steps that produced the answer. Did the agent call the right tools with the right arguments?" -- and a held-out human or LLM-judge pass over edge cases is a second, separate write onto the same record type, not a different data shape: "human annotation to calibrate both."

evidence.quote: Run a curated benchmark against every candidate version in CI and gate the release on the results.
**Trajectory evaluation.** Score the sequence of steps that produced the answer. Did the agent call the right tools with the right arguments?

gaps.what: This card (6.2 Evaluation Data, in Observe) and card 7.3 Evaluate (Blind) (in Self-Improvement) are not cleanly separated by the evidence gathered here. 7.3's own subtitle ('Hidden test sets - Prevent gaming') names a specific practice -- keeping part of the case set unseen by whoever tunes a candidate -- documented in real competitions: a hidden holdout set of games released only after a competition window closes. This card, by contrast, is the general data plane: whatever scores, test results and human feedback an evaluation produces. Nothing in the evidence gathered here states whether a 7.3 hidden-set verdict is stored as an ordinary 6.2 record, or is deliberately withheld from the general data store so the hidden set itself never leaks back to whoever is being evaluated.
gaps.why_it_matters: If the two cards are not separated by a stated rule, a caller cannot tell whether writing every evaluation verdict to one common data store (this card) would itself defeat 7.3's own anti-gaming purpose by exposing the hidden set's answers through the data plane meant to record them.
gaps.research_query: does compose-improvement-loop's own schema, or cap-evaluation's own operations, say whether a hidden-set verdict is excluded from the general evaluation-data store

gaps.what: 'Human feedback' is one of two things this card's own subtitle names, but only one sourced sentence gathered here touches it at all -- 'you can ensemble or human-review the edge cases' -- and it describes human review as an adjunct to LLM-as-judge scoring, not a separate capture mechanism (a rating, an annotation queue, a thumbs up/down). No sourced evidence distinguishes this from cap-human-interaction's own approval/steering contract, which already owns a person entering a run and answering on a correlation id.
gaps.why_it_matters: If 'human feedback' as evaluation data and cap-human-interaction's own approval/answer mechanism are the same underlying event captured twice under two different card names, this card's subtitle may be claiming a concept that already has an owner elsewhere in the reference model.
gaps.research_query: does cap-human-interaction's own event stream ever get written into an evaluation case set or score record, or are the two kept structurally separate

gaps.what: The only standard on this card governs the wire carrier for an already-decided verdict (gen_ai.evaluation.result). No standard covers the rubric definition, scoring thresholds, or case-set versioning scheme itself -- those are entirely this repo's own or a vendor framework's design, with no cited external specification.
gaps.why_it_matters: A card whose only standard covers how a result is transmitted, not how it is produced, means the actual evaluation methodology (what counts as a passing score) is unstandardized and framework-specific, which is a different and larger gap than a missing carrier would be.
gaps.research_query: is there a published, framework-neutral rubric or scoring-threshold standard for agent evaluation as of 2027, beyond the OTel result carrier

gaps.what: This card's definition and usage previously rested on a 'four dimensions: trajectory, tool use, task completion, multi-turn quality' taxonomy cited to morphllm.com. On direct re-fetch, none of those phrases appear anywhere on that 19.8KB page; its own stated framework is three layers -- final-answer, trajectory, and per-turn evaluation -- shown as its own stat-tile callout ('3 layers / Final-answer, trajectory, per-turn'). Separately, the Langfuse product-description quote in this card's tools section was cited to langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview, a page whose full text never carries that sentence at all (it is homepage-style copy). Both citations have been repaired: the definition and usage now cite morphllm.com's genuine three-layer framing, and the Langfuse quote is now cited to langfuse.com's actual homepage.
gaps.why_it_matters: This card's central taxonomy was fabricated relative to its own cited source -- not a minor wording slip but a different number of categories with different names. Any downstream skill or example that adopted the 'four dimensions' vocabulary from this card should be checked against the corrected three-layer framing.
gaps.research_query: does compose-improvement-loop or any example under examples/ reference the old 'trajectory, tool use, task completion, multi-turn quality' four-dimension vocabulary, and if so does it need updating to match this card's corrected three-layer framing
